comment: Files that build a TENANT-rooted storage key (`tenants/<t>/…`), classified. PLAN-spaces.md §1b nests exactly one boundary, so a key written above it is either deliberate (`tenant-level`: the bytes belong to the tenant, above every space) or a recorded finding (`debt`: the owner has space-scoped rows and its bytes have not followed yet). The guard is scripts/check-space-storage-scope.mjs. It reads each owner's migrations for `space_id`, so a `tenant-level` entry whose module later gains a space column becomes an error — that is the mechanism, not the list.

allow.reason: Defines the tenant root of each bucket — the segment every other key hangs off, space-rooted ones included. apps/core owns core.spaces, so the space_id escalation fires on it by construction; this one file is exempt, not the app.
Picks the root by spaceId: fileStorageSpaceObjectKey when a space is present, tenant root only for tenant-level syncs. The tenant branch is the fallback, not the default.
Skills are a tenant-wide library shared across spaces (§1b: `tenants/<t>/ai/skills/…` explicitly stays tenant-level).
Read-only skill mount paths for the tenant skill library.
One company profile per tenant — logo and brand assets are above every space by definition.
Document templates are tenant-wide branding, used by every space; the module has no space-scoped rows.

Expense receipts belong to the tenant's bookkeeping, not to a space: module_expenses scopes its rows by (tenant_id, scope_id) and has no space_id column, and every expenses operation is tenant_shared. If the module gains a space column this entry becomes an error, which is the point.
The copilot's per-user home. §1b keeps the personal home at the tenant root on purpose — it follows the person across spaces, not the space.
Creates the same per-user home prefix.
The tenant file browser: builds and validates the tenant root itself. A space's file space is reached through module_files owners (fileSpaceOwnerPath), not through this path builder.
